boundary_rationale: “Yahweh's law is perfect, restoring the soul” (web:Ps.19.7) opens the torah-panel by naming the covenant name יְהוָ֣ה, Yahweh (oshb:Ps.19.8), which recurs seven times across four verses in this panel — web:Ps.19.7, Ps.19.8, Ps.19.9, and Ps.19.14 (sweep: 7 occurrences across 4 verses, confirmed by sweep.py --skel's verse hits and the whole-psalm inventory's yhwh:7 total) — against the one אֵ֑ל token of the panel before it (oshb:Ps.19.2). Three verses of synonym-paired praise for the law (law/covenant at web:Ps.19.7, precepts/commandment at web:Ps.19.8, fear/ordinances at web:Ps.19.9) run through “sweeter also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb” (web:Ps.19.10) before “Moreover your servant is warned by them” (web:Ps.19.11) turns from describing the law's qualities to the psalmist's own response, closing on the prayer formula “Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, Yahweh, my rock, and my redeemer” (web:Ps.19.14), which readdresses Yahweh directly and closes the psalm.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this panel at web:Ps.19.10|Ps.19.11 carries a tier-1 rival the one-panel reading does not fully answer: web:Ps.19.11 (oshb:Ps.19.12) opens on עַ֭בְדְּךָ (“your servant”), the psalm’s first second-person form, against the third-person law-description running web:Ps.19.7-Ps.19.10 (oshb:Ps.19.8-Ps.19.11), where no second-person form stands. The one-panel reading holds on the strophe’s ~4-8 verse norm and the unbroken movement from the law’s praise into the closing prayer at web:Ps.19.14, not on the sevenfold divine-name count, which is silent across this seam (zero occurrences at oshb:Ps.19.11-Ps.19.14).
observed_substrate_signals: יְהוָ֣ה (Yahweh) occurs twice each at oshb:Ps.19.8, oshb:Ps.19.9, oshb:Ps.19.10 and once at oshb:Ps.19.15 — seven token-occurrences across four verses (sweep: 7 occurrences across 4 verses)
no divine-name token (Yahweh or El) appears at web:Ps.19.11-Ps.19.13, the personal-response verses between the law's praise and the closing prayer formula
device_notes: No selah interrupts web:Ps.19.7-Ps.19.14; this torah panel and the heavens panel that precedes it remain one composition's two internal movements, not separate parents.

boundary_rationale: The title “By David; when he pretended to be insane before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed” opens the psalm at web:Ps.34.0 (oshb:Ps.34.1) — title material naming the Abimelech episode, not a narrative row. Psalm 34 is acrostic (psalm_device_inventory.json: waw absent from the letter sequence) beginning אֲבָרֲכָ֣ה אֶת יְהוָ֣ה בְּכָל עֵ֑ת (oshb:Ps.34.2) “I will bless Yahweh at all times” (web:Ps.34.1), alef; בַּ֭יהוָה תִּתְהַלֵּ֣ל נַפְשִׁ֑י (oshb:Ps.34.3) “My soul shall boast in Yahweh” (web:Ps.34.2), bet; גַּדְּל֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה אִתִּ֑י (oshb:Ps.34.4) “Oh magnify Yahweh with me” (web:Ps.34.3), gimel — a communal invitation opening the strophe.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging web:Ps.34.1-3 with web:Ps.34.4-7 was rejected: the communal invitation register (‘with me’, ‘let’s exalt’ together) closes at web:Ps.34.3 — the psalm’s one 1cp cohortative, וּנְרוֹמְמָ֖ה (oshb:Ps.34.4 = web:Ps.34.3), stands inside this row’s own span and no cohortative of either person recurs from web:Ps.34.4 on — and web:Ps.34.4 turns instead to individual singular testimony, “I sought Yahweh, and he answered me”
observed_substrate_signals: the strophe's three verses open the acrostic's first three letters alef, bet, gimel (byte-checked against web:Ps.34.1-3; sweep: 22 verses, waw the acrostic's only gap per psalm_device_inventory.json)

וּנְרוֹמְמָ֖ה שְׁמ֣וֹ יַחְדָּֽו (oshb:Ps.34.4) closes the strophe on the cohortative “Let's exalt his name together” (web:Ps.34.3), the final plural-cohortative verb before individual testimony resumes
device_notes: Psalm 34's rows answer to one shared parent grouping across this part. The historical title names Abimelech (1 Sam 21 material, kept as title text and not quoted as narrative); the acrostic surface is byte-confirmed alef through gimel here and continues waw-less through this psalm's remaining rows.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens on direct imperative address to Yahweh, רִיבָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה אֶת יְרִיבַ֑י (oshb:Ps.35.1) “Contend, Yahweh, with those who contend with me.” (web:Ps.35.1), and runs an imprecation against the psalmist’s pursuers through web:Ps.35.8; it turns at web:Ps.35.9-Ps.35.10 into a vow spoken in the psalmist’s own voice, וְ֭נַפְשִׁי תָּגִ֣יל (oshb:Ps.35.9) “My soul shall be joyful in Yahweh.” (web:Ps.35.9), a petition-to-vow turn that recurs as the close of this psalm’s two later complaint cycles (web:Ps.35.18, web:Ps.35.27-Ps.35.28).
strongest_rejected_alternative: web:Ps.35.9-Ps.35.10 could stand as its own short vow unit, but the addressee and subject stay the same as web:Ps.35.1-Ps.35.8, so it reads as this cycle's close rather than a fresh movement.
observed_substrate_signals: imperative verbs cluster at the open, רִיבָ֣ה (oshb:Ps.35.1) “Contend”, הַחֲזֵ֣ק (oshb:Ps.35.2) “Take hold”, וְהָ֘רֵ֤ק (oshb:Ps.35.3) “Brandish” (web:Ps.35.1-Ps.35.3)
the vow verbs תָּגִ֣יל and תָּ֝שִׂישׂ (oshb:Ps.35.9) replace the imprecative mood of web:Ps.35.4-Ps.35.8
device_notes: All of Psalm 35's rows meet in one parent. The psalm runs three petition-to-vow cycles closing at web:Ps.35.9-Ps.35.10, web:Ps.35.18, and web:Ps.35.27-Ps.35.28; this row covers the opening cycle.

boundary_rationale: web:Ps.37.20 opens, “But the wicked shall perish.”; its surface letter כ sits at the position expected for kaf, though the word is the particle כִּ֤י (oshb:Ps.37.20, “for/but”) rather than a content word. web:Ps.37.21 opens on ל (לֹוֶ֣ה, oshb:Ps.37.21, “borrows”), positioned earlier than a strict two-verse-per-letter count would predict — the acrostic's own known irregularity in this zone. מ opens web:Ps.37.23, “A man’s steps are established by Yahweh.” The content maintains the same wicked-versus-righteous contrast across all 5 verses of the span: רָ֭שָׁע (‘wicked’, oshb:Ps.37.21) and וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק (“but the righteous”, oshb:Ps.37.21) appear together at web:Ps.37.21, and the related plural רְשָׁעִ֨ים (‘the wicked’, oshb:Ps.37.20) stands as the second word of the span's first verse, web:Ps.37.20, immediately after the kaf particle כִּ֤י (oshb:Ps.37.20) (“the wicked… The enemies of Yahweh”); the same opposition continues under different vocabulary at web:Ps.37.22 (“blessed by him”/“cursed by him”), and web:Ps.37.23-24 (the righteous individual's steps established by Yahweh) — corroborating the row's outer bounds even where the letter sequence itself is irregular.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A stricter reading would open a new row at web:Ps.37.21 to line up with lamed's letter position, but the wicked-versus-righteous contrast running web:Ps.37.20-Ps.37.24 is one content movement, so the letter irregularity is disclosed here rather than used to force an extra row.
observed_substrate_signals: surface כ at web:Ps.37.20 sits on the causal particle כִּ֤י (oshb:Ps.37.20), not a fresh content word — a byte-checked irregularity in the acrostic's surface letter sequence
ל opens web:Ps.37.21 one verse earlier than a regular two-verse kaf span would predict — a documented irregularity, not asserted as a clean letter-pair
device_notes: An irregular front-half zone of the acrostic (kaf/lamed compressed around web:Ps.37.20-Ps.37.22); the row is content-driven, with the letter table carried as corroboration. The surface letter at web:Ps.37.20 sits on the causal particle כִּ֤י (oshb:Ps.37.20) rather than a fresh content word, and lamed opens one verse earlier than the acrostic's usual two-verse-per-letter pattern would predict — a byte-derived irregularity, re-checked directly from the verse text rather than sourced to any editorial caveat.

boundary_rationale: Past the oracle’s divine first-person speech, which closes at oshb:Ps.60.10 (web:Ps.60.8), this unit opens with the psalmist’s own voice resuming in a question, (oshb:Ps.60.11) מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי “Who will bring me into the strong city?” (web:Ps.60.9), moves through the renewed complaint “Haven’t you, God, rejected us?” (web:Ps.60.10) and the petition “Give us help against the adversary” (web:Ps.60.11), and closes on communal resolve, “Through God we will do valiantly” (web:Ps.60.12), closing the psalm at its twelfth WEB verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this closing unit at the shift from the singular 'me' of Ps.60.9 to the communal 'us' of Ps.60.10 was rejected, since no independent tier-1 driver marks that pronoun shift as a fresh strophe boundary rather than one continuous closing movement.
observed_substrate_signals: Interrogative resumption at web:Ps.60.9 (oshb:Ps.60.11) follows the oracle’s divine first-person speech, which closes at oshb:Ps.60.10, and precedes the second-person address to God opening at oshb:Ps.60.12 (web:Ps.60.10).
Span covers the psalm’s last 4 verses, closing at web:Ps.60.12 (oshb:Ps.60.14), the final MT verse of Ps 60.
device_notes: This span continues the material shared with Psalm 108, noted where the oracle closes (web:Ps.60.8); disclosed here as a typed relation, not a boundary driver.

boundary_rationale: Past the psalm's refrain return at oshb:Ps.62.7 (= web:Ps.62.6), whose opening five tokens repeat oshb:Ps.62.3 byte-for-byte, this unit opens still in first-person voice, continuing the rock vocabulary of that refrain's close: “My salvation and my honor is with God. The rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God.” (web:Ps.62.7), where OSHB's צוּר עֻזִּ֥י (“rock of my strength”, oshb:Ps.62.8) echoes the refrain's own צ֭וּרִי. One verse in, register shifts to public exhortation: (oshb:Ps.62.9) בִּטְח֘וּ ב֤וֹ בְכָל עֵ֨ת עָ֗ם “Trust in him at all times, you people” (web:Ps.62.8), closing on the psalm’s second Selah. The unit moves through the wisdom reflection on human vanity, “men of low degree are just a breath” (web:Ps.62.9), and the warning against riches (web:Ps.62.10), closing on the revelatory formula (oshb:Ps.62.12) אַחַ֤ת דִּבֶּ֬ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים שְׁתַּֽיִם “God has spoken once; twice I have heard this” (web:Ps.62.11).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Ps.62.7-62.8 as a continuation of the preceding confidence refrain rather than a fresh public-facing unit was rejected, given the shift from first-person soul-address to plural imperative address.
observed_substrate_signals: Plural imperative address (oshb:Ps.62.9) בִּטְח֘וּ opens the exhortation, marking the register shift from the preceding first-person ring.
Selah closes web:Ps.62.8 (oshb:Ps.62.9) — the psalm’s later of 2 Selah instances (sweep: 2 verses); no further Selah in web:Ps.62.9-web:Ps.62.12.
device_notes: The Hebrew word for "silence" opening (oshb:Ps.62.2) דּֽוּמִיָּ֣ה recurs, from the same root, at the opening of oshb:Ps.65.2 (web:Ps.65.1) — shared vocabulary texture, not a boundary signal.

boundary_rationale: The historical address opens on the wilderness march, “God, when you went out before your people, when you marched through the wilderness” (web:Ps.68.7), closed by a Selah, and continues through Sinai theophany imagery, “The earth trembled. The sky also poured down rain at the presence of the God of Sinai” (web:Ps.68.8), into a battle report whose vocabulary is genuinely obscure: “She who waits at home divides the plunder” (web:Ps.68.12), “the wings of a dove sheathed with silver, her feathers with shining gold” (web:Ps.68.13), plus “it snowed on Zalmon” (web:Ps.68.14). The strophe is bounded by the vocative-plus-Selah opening at web:Ps.68.7 and the scene shift at web:Ps.68.15 (= oshb:Ps.68.16), a verbless third-person mountain chain whose הַ֥ר גַּ֝בְנֻנִּ֗ים is picked up by the vocative direct address opening one verse later at web:Ps.68.16 (= oshb:Ps.68.17); its interior (web:Ps.68.9-web:Ps.68.14) resists a finer tier-1 split — the identity of the home-waiting figure and the referent of the silver-dove and Zalmon-snow images are argued in the commentary tradition, not settled by the bytes available here.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting web:Ps.68.7-web:Ps.68.14 at web:Ps.68.11 (“The Lord announced the word”) into a Sinai-theophany half and a battle-report half was rejected: web:Ps.68.11's declarative sentence continues the same historical narration. 2nd-person address to God does stop at web:Ps.68.11 itself (0 of 6 tokens in the staged extract there carry 2ms forms [web:Ps.68.11 = oshb:Ps.68.12], against 3 of the preceding 4 verses [web:Ps.68.7-web:Ps.68.10 = oshb:Ps.68.8-Ps.68.11]), a genuine addressee shift disclosed here as the strongest rival candidate; it is held at this row's own medium_low confidence rather than adopted, absent a second independent tier-1 signal at that seam.
observed_substrate_signals: Vocative address “God, when you went out” opens the strophe with a Selah closing web:Ps.68.7.
Theophanic vocabulary (earth trembling, rain, Sinai) runs web:Ps.68.8-web:Ps.68.9.

The battle-report vocabulary at web:Ps.68.12-web:Ps.68.14 (plunder, dove wings, Zalmon snow) draws on terms this psalm does not repeat elsewhere in its own bounds; no internal imperative or vocative shift subdivides it at the byte level available.

boundary_rationale: Psalm 78 opens with a maskil superscription (“A contemplation by Asaph.”, web:Ps.78.0) sitting inside the same MT verse as the psalm's opening imperative, then unfolds one continuous wisdom exordium: the call “Hear my teaching, my people. Turn your ears to the words of my mouth.” (web:Ps.78.1) sets a teacher's address that a purpose-clause chain develops — the covenant-transmission command of web:Ps.78.5, extended by “that the generation to come might know…who should arise and tell their children” (web:Ps.78.6) and “that they might set their hope in God, and not forget God's deeds, but keep his commandments” (web:Ps.78.7) — until it resolves in a negative exemplar, “and might not be as their fathers- a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation that didn't make their hearts loyal, whose spirit was not steadfast with God.” (web:Ps.78.8). The unnamed “fathers” of web:Ps.78.8 are then given a specific referent at web:Ps.78.9, marking the seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A break after web:Ps.78.4’s transmission pledge was considered but rejected because oshb:Ps.78.5 opens on the wayyiqtol וַיָּ֤קֶם, switching the subject to God’s own commissioning act, while the transmission vocabulary of oshb:Ps.78.4 — לְד֥וֹר אַחֲר֗וֹן, מְֽ֭סַפְּרִים, מִבְּנֵיהֶ֗ם — recurs across the seam in דּ֣וֹר אַ֭חֲרוֹן, וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ and לִבְנֵיהֶֽם (also closing oshb:Ps.78.5 as לִבְנֵיהֶֽם) through oshb:Ps.78.5-Ps.78.6, and the purpose-clause chain then runs from oshb:Ps.78.6 to the negative exemplar at web:Ps.78.8.
observed_substrate_signals: the superscription מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ף (web:Ps.78.0 = oshb:Ps.78.1, byte tier) sits inside MT v1 before the body clause הַאֲזִ֣ינָה עַ֭מִּי תּוֹרָתִ֑י (oshb:Ps.78.1, byte tier), consistent with this psalm's identity numbering

the purpose-clause particle opening web:Ps.78.6 (לְמַ֤עַן, oshb:Ps.78.6, byte tier) chains forward from the covenant-commission of web:Ps.78.5; web:Ps.78.7 continues the same purpose clause on a plain waw-conjunctive verb (וְיָשִׂ֥ימוּ, oshb:Ps.78.7, byte tier) rather than opening a fresh particle of its own
web:Ps.78.8 closes on an unnamed collective (“their fathers”) that web:Ps.78.9 immediately specifies by tribal name — a subject change unlike any within web:Ps.78.1-web:Ps.78.8
device_notes: Psalm 78's title carries the maskil and le-Asaph genre labels (web:Ps.78.0 = oshb:Ps.78.1).
